chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yāsīn, from Ḥarīz and Ibn Miskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked him about a dhimmī who cut off the hand of a Muslim.

He said: "His hand is cut off, if his heirs wish, and they take the difference between the two blood-monies. And if the Muslim cuts off the hand of the muʿāhad, the heirs of the muʿāhad are given the choice: if they wish, they take the blood-money for his hand; and if they wish, they cut off the hand of the Muslim and pay him the difference between the two blood-monies. And if the Muslim kills him, it is done likewise."

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ: his legal heirs or entitled guardians who may exercise the claim
key_terms.الدِّيَتَيْنِ: the two blood-monies being compared in compensation
key_terms.الْمُعَاهَدِ: a non-Muslim under covenant or treaty protection
key_terms.تُقْطَعُ: it is cut off, referring here to retaliatory amputation in qiṣāṣ
key_terms.دِيَةَ: financial compensation due for bodily injury or killing
key_terms.ذِمِّيٍّ: a non-Muslim living under the protection covenant of the Islamic polity
key_terms.فَضْلَ: the excess or difference payable between two amounts

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of qiṣāṣ and diyah when a dhimmī or muʿāhad is injured or killed by a Muslim, or vice versa?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings of qiṣāṣ and diyah between a Muslim and a non-Muslim under covenant, including a dhimmī and a muʿāhad. It explains the heirs' options in cases of bodily injury and killing, along with payment of the difference between the two blood-monies where applicable.
